findings.title: WebView setAllowFileAccess(true) under system UID context
findings.rationale: On API 30+ the default is false; the explicit opt-in re-enables file:// scheme access. The hosting APK declares android:sharedUserId=android.uid.system and uses-permission WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, so a controllable htmlContentPath could read privileged system files via file:// URLs.

findings.title: WebView.loadUrl(htmlContentPath) without scheme or origin validation
findings.rationale: htmlContentPath is the function parameter and is forwarded to loadUrl with no allow-list, scheme check, or asset prefix. Combined with setAllowFileAccess(true) and the system UID, an untrusted caller could induce file:// or javascript: navigations. Caller trust boundary is not visible in this file — needs follow-up to identify producers.

findings.title: Implicit broadcast carries response payload (status/message/response JSON) without setPackage or signature permission
findings.rationale: The action string is custom but the broadcast is implicit (no setPackage, no signature-protected receiver permission). Any app on the device that registers a receiver for this action observes the response. Under system UID, this is a one-way information channel out of the system process. If the response ever contains user-context (Gleo voice command results, vehicle property values), it is exposed to third-party apps.

findings.title: Untrusted Intent extra `macAddress` is persisted to the paired-device repository without validation
findings.rationale: If this receiver is exported (manifest declares several android:exported='true' receivers — needs cross-check), an attacker can broadcast `DEVICE_SUPPORT_ANDROID_AUTO_WIRELESS` with an arbitrary `macAddress` string and inject DB rows under the system UID. No format validation, no signature-permission gate visible at the call site.

findings.title: registerReceiver without RECEIVER_EXPORTED/RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED flag (UnspecifiedRegisterReceiverFlag suppressed)
findings.rationale: On Android 14+ (target API 34) explicit `RECEIVER_EXPORTED`/`RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED` is required. The lint suppression keeps the legacy default which, for system apps with `INTERNET` permission, can register an exported receiver implicitly. Each caller of `Broadcasts.observe(...)` inherits this and may be surprised. Severity is low because the *callers* drive the action allow-list, but it widens the attack surface across the codebase.

findings.title: grantRuntimePermission(packageName, ...) on a caller-supplied packageName with no allow-list
findings.rationale: this.packageName is captured from the constructor argument. There is no validation that the targeted package exists, is system-signed, or that the caller has the right to mutate its permissions. Combined with the host APK's system UID and platform signature, this method is effectively a privileged primitive: if any reachable code path lets an untrusted producer choose packageName, an attacker can promote a third-party APK to runtime permissions it could not otherwise hold.

findings.title: revokeRuntimePermission(packageName, ...) — symmetric primitive without callsite validation
findings.rationale: Same caller-trust issue as grantPermission. An attacker controlling packageName can revoke another app's runtime permissions, potentially silencing security features (e.g. revoke ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION from a safety app).
